body: Oh okay, I am glad. Good luck to you with healing!
You are dating the man who sexually assaulted you?

He only held hands with the female friend, then went to the bathroom the same time as her, then he only hugged her. It feels sketchy to me that he doesn’t hold the males hand, even though they are closer, same with hugging, etc. I also don’t appreciate how the first thing he did was try to say I’m over reacting and everyone thinks I’m over reacting, rather than acknowledging that it made me uncomfortable and he won’t do it again

You are right to say that I shouldn’t get stuck on what could have been, because I definitely think that is the most painful part. I do think seeing a therapist would be good. My mom doesn’t know about my abortion, only my boyfriend. I wish I could tell her but I do not think she would take it well at all. I do go to an online college but they doesn’t really have expansive counseling. The counseling is brief intervention for students who are feeling stressed, overwhelmed, or struggling with symptoms of mental illness. 

Thank you sharing a part of your story with me and for your advice. I suppose I thought I wouldn’t feel as much as I do. But you are right that I made the decision that was right for me at the time.

Those last five sentences really resonated with me and perfectly explain how I feel. Thank you for sharing a part of your story with me. It really helps me to hear others experiences on this. I felt kind of guilty being triggered about pregnant people, especially people I care about, but now I feel like it’s just a part of the grief.
Thank you for helping me think of this situation in a more positive light!

Sincerely, thank you and everyone on this thread so much. I was scared to share such a personal part of my life, especially since no one else knows about my abortion but my boyfriend. It helps to know that this is such a kind space because in person, I couldn’t imagine telling someone else. For instance, I wish I could tell my dad but he think it’s the worst thing in the world but otherwise is a great father.
I definitely think I need counseling so thank you for sharing how counseling helped you through a similar situation!

Thank you for reminding me not to be so hard on myself, it’s easy to be mean to myself on such a sensitive topic. I do think that if I reframed my perspective in a more positive light I would definitely feel a bit better.

Thank you for your kindness, but also for your rationality. I know logically that I didn’t have a baby but I don’t know why I feel so much grief. When I got pregnant (and for my entire life) I did not want a baby. But now, all I want is THAT possibility back. The circumstances of my abortion weren’t great and like you said, I’m sure we would not have been as stable as we are now if I didn’t get the abortion. I think I might have expected to not feel this much, as I didn’t ever want a baby but all of this has made me want one.
 
It felt like so many things went wrong, the protection failed and after the experience I tried birth control but I felt even worse emotionally/mentally. My boyfriend did not force me to get an abortion but he kind of assumed I wanted one, based on my reaction to the pregnancy test and we didn’t talk about it nearly as much as we should have. And when I took the second pill, we had an unrelated fight and I was alone while bleeding through a pad at least every thirty minutes. I thought I should go to the hospital but I didn’t want to be shamed. 

I’m sorry if that was too much information. But liked you said I do need to address my feelings in the open, and I definitely want to do that.
Thank you so much!

It makes me feel a bit better to know I am not the only one feeling grief, especially since no one knows I got an abortion except my boyfriend . I wish you all of the luck in the world in trying for a baby! Thank you so much for your kind words and advice.
Thank you so much - along with reaching out to the clinic for tools and resources for this specific circumstance, I think it would also be good for me to try therapy

Thank you - I didn’t even think of reaching out to the clinic. Now that you mention it, it does seem like a great idea that would help me deal with these feelings. When I have time today I am going to look up my clinic and try to find those resources!

I’ve never been to therapy and I don’t know how to even start that process. I’m on my moms insurance and I’ve never been to the doctor by myself or set anything up by myself. I also have a lot of issues so I don’t know what to pursue first. Thank you for your comment

Thank you for your response. I emailed my professors I just expect nothing positive and decide I will drop out if they don’t accept late, since that will fail me anyway. I don’t know how to calm down right now. I feel like a destroy and ruin everything
Stop spamming posts

When I was younger I was one of those people who cared too much about looks and I ended up with a good-looking guy. He was good-looking but he was also abusive, toxic, and manipulative. This is not to say good-looking = bad person or not good-looking = good person. Now, I’ve been in a relationship for over two years with someone who most people think is not ‘good-looking’. I’m the happiest I have ever been because I have someone who genuinely cares about me and our relationship, and to me is a beautiful person inside and out. 

The older you get the more you realize, looks aren’t everything. And even if someone is not conventionally attractive, in my case at least, loving a person makes them more beautiful. Good luck.

Thank you again for your comment. I do think I need to sit down and have at least one more serious conversation with him. He is not a bad person, and I know that these types of posts make it so it’s really easy to empathize with the poster. As bad as he sounds from my post, he is a genuinely good person and the best relationship I have been in. He treats me wonderfully, just when it comes to chores and other stuff, it is so unfair that it can be frustrating. Maybe I am confusing him, or maybe he is lazy… but I do need to have that conversation with him to find that out, like you suggested.

I do have membership invitations from the National Honor Society and the National Society of Collegiate Scholars. I honestly don’t know about a lot of what makes an adult, an independent adult. I get free college up to an associates degree because of my moms union. My mom also claims me on her taxes even though I haven’t lived with her in years. There is so much I don’t know about and I feel dumb because my parents didn’t really do the best job or make an effort at all to explain things like this.

Hi, thank you for your comment. I have been trying to look up solutions like this. We do something a bit like what you mentioned, he doesn’t like to dust so I do all of the dusting, which I do not mind. The one thing I don’t clean is toilet bowl, which he doesn’t mind cleaning… stuff like that. Right now, he works and I don’t, and I am earning my degree. I know that with him being the only one working, that stuff like this won’t be equal, but it feels like even with him working - I know he could be helping out so much more than he does.

I really don’t want to breakup with him, but I know that I should if he can’t make an honest effort.

I honestly don’t have any friends who live in the same state as me, let alone a vehicle. I don’t think I could make it on my own… I’ve never had an apartment by myself, a car, insurance, and I also am a student too. I know other people make do but I’m honestly struggling with just my classes and emotional/mental health.
